details:
Our project, AI-Powered Astronaut Mental Health Risk Prediction System, is designed to monitor and support the mental well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions.

The system collects information such as mood check-ins, sleep duration, physical activity, stress levels and optional wearable sensor data. It analyses these inputs using AI-based techniques to identify unusual changes in an astronaut's normal behavioural and well-being patterns. Based on the analysis, it provides early-warning alerts, personalized self-care suggestions and recommendations for human support when necessary.

The main benefits of this project are early identification of mental health risks, improved astronaut well-being, better mission performance and reduced psychological difficulties caused by isolation, confinement and workload. Our aim is to create a safer and healthier environment for astronauts during space exploration.

For the proposed prototype, we plan to use Python, Streamlit or React, SQLite, Pandas and Scikit-learn for data processing, analysis and dashboard development. The creative aspect of our project is its personalized prediction approach, which compares each astronaut's current condition with their individual normal baseline rather than using the same standard for everyone.

We also considered important factors such as data privacy, security, accuracy, ethical AI use and human supervision. This system is intended as an early-warning support tool and not as a medical diagnostic system.
